title: Contrast and concession
tagline: Say two things pull in different directions — with a clause, a noun, or a whole new sentence.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 2 — open cloze
why: Every B2 First essay needs to weigh up two sides of an argument, and the linker you choose signals whether what follows is a clause, a noun, or a completely new sentence. Mixing these up — despite + a clause without 'the fact that', or however joined with a comma splice — is one of the most common accuracy errors in Writing Part 1.

diagrams.title: although / even though vs despite / in spite of

rows.label: Followed by
cells: a noun phrase, an -ing form, or 'the fact that' + clause

rows.label: Example
cells: Although it was raining, we went hiking.
Despite the rain, we went hiking.

rows.label: Position
cells: start or middle of the sentence, comma if first
start or middle of the sentence, comma if first

diagrams.title: despite / in spite of + -ing
diagrams.caption: Despite losing the first set, Nadia won the match.

head: Linker
Followed by
Example
rows: Although she was tired, she finished the race.
Despite the heat, they kept playing.
In spite of losing, the team stayed positive.
despite / in spite of the fact that
Despite the fact that it rained, the match went ahead.
Mateo loves maths, whereas Sofia prefers art.
It was raining. However, we still went out.
balances a second point of view
On the other hand, staying in is safer.
adds a contrast to the previous sentence

examples.text: Although the coach warned them about the wind, the team still went sailing.
Even though she'd never played chess before, Nadia beat the school champion.
Mateo finished the marathon, though he could barely walk afterwards.
examples.note: though at the end of a clause, informal

use.point: Prepositions followed by a noun, -ing or 'the fact that'

examples.text: Despite the traffic, we reached the stadium just in time.
In spite of feeling nervous, Liam gave a confident presentation.
Despite the fact that he'd studied all week, Mateo felt unprepared.
examples.note: the only way to follow despite with a full clause

examples.text: Sofia prefers working in silence, whereas Nadia needs music in the background.
While some students revise alone, others prefer group study sessions.
examples.note: while at the start of a sentence

use.point: Starting a new sentence: however, nevertheless, on the other hand

examples.text: The forecast predicted heavy rain. However, the match went ahead as planned.
The team lost every game this season. Nevertheless, they never stopped training.
Staying up late feels productive. On the other hand, it makes revision harder the next day.

watch_out.wrong: Despite it was raining, we went to the beach.
watch_out.right: Despite the rain, we went to the beach. / Although it was raining, we went to the beach.
watch_out.why: Despite is a preposition — it cannot be followed directly by a subject and verb.

watch_out.wrong: In spite of the fact it was late, she called back.
watch_out.right: In spite of the fact that it was late, she called back.
watch_out.why: Before a full clause you need the complete phrase 'the fact that', not just 'the fact'.

watch_out.wrong: It was raining, however we still went out.
watch_out.right: It was raining. However, we still went out.
watch_out.why: However joins ideas across two sentences (or after a semicolon), not with a comma splice.

watch_out.wrong: Despite of the cold, they kept training.
watch_out.why: Despite never takes 'of' — only in spite of does.

watch_out.wrong: Although the storm, the flight left on time.
watch_out.right: Although there was a storm, the flight left on time. / Despite the storm, the flight left on time.
watch_out.why: Although needs a full clause; use despite/in spite of before a noun.

watch_out.wrong: Liam is confident, meanwhile Sofia gets nervous before exams.
watch_out.right: Liam is confident, whereas Sofia gets nervous before exams.
watch_out.why: Meanwhile is about time, not contrast — whereas or while is what's needed here.

dialogue.title: Two ways to prepare for the debate
dialogue.context: Sofia and Liam disagree about how to prepare for the school debate, and Miss Vega joins in with some advice.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Although we've only got two days left, I think we should still rewrite the opening.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Despite the time pressure, I actually think the opening is fine as it is.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Maybe. Whereas you focus on delivery, I care more about the actual arguments.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Fair point. In spite of disagreeing about the opening, we do agree on the main argument.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: True. Even though the topic is difficult, our research is solid.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good. Nevertheless, I'd practise the timing again — you both ran over last time.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: We will. Sofia prefers rehearsing alone, while I like practising in front of people.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Despite the fact that that makes me nervous, maybe I should try your way once.

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Good idea. On the other hand, don't change your whole method two days before the debate.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Fine. Tiring week, though, whichever way we prepare.

practice.instructions: Complete each sentence with although, even though, despite, in spite of, whereas or however.

items.sentence: ___ the long queue, they managed to get tickets for the final.
___ it was freezing outside, the students still trained on the field.
Nadia loves early mornings, ___ Sofia can barely get out of bed before nine.
The exam was difficult. ___, most of the class passed.
___ feeling nervous, Mateo answered every question calmly.
___ she studies every day, Sofia still finds grammar difficult.
___ the fact that the trip was cancelled, nobody complained.
He plays the guitar well, ___ he's never had a proper lesson.

summary: Although, even though and though are conjunctions: they need a subject and a verb.
Despite and in spite of are prepositions: they need a noun, an -ing form, or 'the fact that' + clause.
Whereas and while set two ideas directly against each other, usually in one sentence.
However, nevertheless and on the other hand start a new sentence (or follow a semicolon) — never a comma splice.
In Part 4, the key word usually tells you whether the answer needs a clause or a noun phrase after it.
